active: Captain Ralden
Wayfarer. Crownsfall stands, but barely. The Whisperwood east of the gate has turned — things walk there that remember nothing but hunger.
The Archive's last pages were carried into that wood when the old wardens fell. Without them, the city forgets itself. Will you bring them back?

ready.objective: Return the pages to Captain Ralden

ready: Captain Ralden
Three pages, whole and unburnt. You have done what a company of my soldiers could not.
But these pages name something else — a warden of the wood who did not fall. The Thornwarden still stands in the meadow at the wood's heart. End it, and the Whisperwood is ours again.
active: Captain Ralden
The pages are held by the wood's guardians: in the Flower Dell to the south-west, at the Fae Ring to the south, and among the Standing Stones in the north-east. Check your map (M).

active.objective: Descend beneath the Standing Stones and end the Barrow-Lord

ready.objective: Tell Captain Ralden the barrow is quiet

active: Captain Ralden
One more thing about those pages: the script on them matches the carvings on the Standing Stones in the Whisperwood's north-east.
The stones were opened last week. Something climbed out. There is a stair down to an old barrow. Its lord was buried before Crownsfall had a name. Put him back.
ready: Captain Ralden
A tomb older than the city, and armour no smith of ours could make.
The more we dig, the less we seem to know about who came before us. Take this.

active.objective: Slay the Thornwarden in the Mossy Meadow

active: Captain Ralden
The Thornwarden waits in the Mossy Meadow, at the end of the trail south of the glade. Rest, mend your gear, then go.
ready: Captain Ralden
It is done, then. The Whisperwood is quiet for the first time in a generation.
Hollowmere lies beyond it — and whatever drowned it. When you are ready, Crownsfall will need you again.

epilogue.title: THE WHISPERWOOD IS FREE
lines: The Thornwarden has fallen and the old wood breathes again.
But the pages speak of the marsh beyond: the wardens' lanterns in Hollowmere have gone dark, and something below the water is waking.
Chapter II begins: cross the mossy arch in the Whisperwood's south-east into Hollowmere.

active.objective: Cross the Mossy Arch into Hollowmere

active: Captain Ralden
The Thornwarden was only a gatekeeper. Beyond the mossy arch in the Whisperwood's south-east lies Hollowmere, where the wardens once kept their lanterns burning against the dark water.
The lanterns are out. Whatever drowned the wardens is rising. Go through the arch and see what is left.

ready.objective: Bring the flames to Captain Ralden

active: Captain Ralden
Each lantern held a warden's flame. Whatever guards them now took them when the lanterns died: the Reed-Mother in the north, the Willow Hag in the south, the Bonekeeper on the isle of bones.
Take the flames back. The Ferryman's Rest waypoint will bring you home and back again.
ready: Captain Ralden
Three flames, still burning. The wardens kept these alive for three hundred years.
They burn toward the east, toward the Sunken Chapel. Something there drowned the wardens, and it is still down there. End it.

active.objective: Destroy the Drowned Matron in the Sunken Chapel

epilogue.title: THE MERE IS STILL
lines: The Drowned Matron sinks for the last time and the wardens' lanterns burn again across Hollowmere.
But the flames lean east. Beyond the marsh an old causeway runs over the salt heath toward the harbour of Saltmarrow, and brigands hold its toll.
Chapter III begins: take the Greyfen road out of Hollowmere's north-east.

active: Captain Ralden
The Sunken Chapel lies at the far east of the mere, where the boardwalk ends. Mend your gear, then go.
ready: Captain Ralden
The mere is quiet? Then the wardens can rest at last.
But Saltmarrow's ships have stopped coming. The causeway east is held by a brigand who calls himself the Tollkeeper. Take this, and take the road.

active.objective: Take the causeway out of Hollowmere's north-east

active: Captain Ralden
Hollowmere's north-east edge climbs onto the old wardens' causeway. Follow it east over the Greyfen to Saltmarrow.

active.objective: Break the Tollkeeper's hold on the Toll Tower

active: Harbourmaster Wenna
You came over the causeway? Then you saw the Toll Tower. The Tollkeeper bleeds every cart that passes. Nothing has reached us in a month.
ready: Harbourmaster Wenna
The Tollkeeper is dead? Then the carts will roll again by morning.
Saltmarrow will not forget it. Take this, and rest by our fire.

active.objective: Recover the lighthouse lenses on the Wreckers' Strand

ready.objective: Bring the lenses to Harbourmaster Wenna

active: Harbourmaster Wenna

Our lighthouse went dark the night the wardens' lanterns did. The wreckers stripped its three lenses and took them up the Strand: one to the tide pools, one to the wreck of the Gilded Oath, one to the smugglers' cave.
Bring them back and the ships can find us again.
ready: Harbourmaster Wenna
All three lenses, and not a crack in them.
When we lit the lamp last night, the beam swung east on its own and stopped on Warden's Rock. Something out there wanted the light to go out.

active.objective: Face what waits on Warden's Rock

epilogue.title: THE WARDEN WHO CAME BACK
lines: The Tidewrought Warden wore armour no smith alive could make, and spoke a language only the Archive Pages still hold.
He did not drown in our time. Something brought him here: a tear in the hours beneath the Strand, in the smugglers' deep grotto, where the sea runs the wrong way.
The Age of the Lost has forgotten what came before it. The past has not forgotten us.

active: Harbourmaster Wenna
Warden's Rock is at the far end of the Strand. The old folk say a warden kept the sea-lantern there once. Go carefully.
ready: Harbourmaster Wenna
A warden, in armour like nothing from any forge I know. And you say he talked as if the Concord still stood?
The smugglers have been selling trinkets like his for months. They come from a grotto under the Strand. Take this, and be careful what you find down there.
